messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight 'capability token' for service-to-service auth to reduce API key blast radius and simplify per-route RBAC. Short-lived, signed, optionally bound to org/project and route claims.
ajay: Interesting. Two quick Qs: 1) latency/CPU cost for per-request signature checks? 2) migration for high-QPS services?
sasha: Love the security posture but worried about churn. Many backend jobs use long-lived keys. Need a backwards-compatible path.
ken: Implementation sketch: central minting broker (auth-broker) issues short TTL JWTs signed by HSM. Validators use cached JWKs to avoid hitting HSM on every request. Typical TTL 60-900s.
emily: Rollout plan suggestion: opt-in per-route flag. For canary, accept both API keys and capability tokens, but log acceptance reasons. After one week of good metrics, flip to reject-old-keys for that route.
maria: Tradeoffs: + reduces lateral movement, + maps neatly to route-level privileges. - Adds broker + rotation complexity, - need robust JWK distribution. Must measure CPU for verification.
ajay: For QPS, consider symmetric (HMAC) tokens for internal-only paths to avoid asymmetric verify costs. Also use hardware crypto and cached verifiers.
sasha: Migration checklist request: 1) broker API spec, 2) client libs (go/py), 3) JWK distribution + rotation playbook, 4) phased opt-in + canary, 5) enforcement tooling.
ken: Edge case: offline batch workers with no network to refresh tokens. Proposal: allow bounded long-lived project-scoped tokens with stricter rotation and audit. Also add tenant-affinity claim to reduce cross-tenant reuse risk.
emily: Observability: emit X-Accepted-Credential header value, token-type, minting-principal, route-claim, audit-id. Add auto-rollback: if error rate >5% during canary, temporarily revert to accept-api-key mode.
maria: Security detail: should org/project be embedded in token or derived? I prefer embedding org/project and audience claim so validation is cheap and intent explicit.
ajay: Agree embed, but broker must produce attestation binding token to service identity and routes. Also include region/origins claim to prevent replay across regions.
sasha: Perf test plan: benchmark 10k rps for HMAC vs RSA/EC verify, measure p95 latency and CPU. Also simulate JWK rotation churn to measure cache invalidation effects.
ken: SDK draft example:
```
POST /v1/mint
{ "service": "ingest-worker", "routes": ["/v1/ingest"], "ttl": 300 }
// token claims:
{ "iss":"auth-broker", "sub":"svc:ingest-worker", "aud":"/v1/ingest", "org":"org-123", "exp":1749201534 }
```
ops-bot: Feature-flag created: `capability-auth` in staging. Use `ff toggle capability-auth on --env=staging` to opt-in.
emily: Can we standardize a compatibility header `X-Accepted-Credential: api-key|capability` to simplify logs and metrics?
maria: Yes — include that in SDKs and server middleware.
ken: Next actions: I'll draft broker API + JWK rotation doc. Sasha, own migration playbook. Emily, own canary + rollback wiring. Ajay, own perf harness. Maria will write security appendix for attestation semantics.
sasha: Got it. I'll draft playbook with timelines and offline-worker mitigations.
ajay: Starting perf harness tomorrow, will share findings by EOW.
emily: I'll add observability checkboxes to the rollout checklist.
maria: If no blockers, I'll open a short RFC PR tomorrow with broker API and migration outline. :thumbsup:
